I am a 52-year-old woman. I only finished primary school, but I have been farming these 8 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. My household has seven people — my husband, my son and daughter-in-law, their two children, and my elderly mother. My son works construction in Shijiazhuang and sends home about 5,000 yuan a year. That money is important, but I still watch every yuan I spend on the farm. I learn mostly from my own experience and from watching my neighbors. Auntie Liu down the road farms about the same as me, and we talk at the well when we are both irrigating.

This year I will manage my land the same way I always do, because change is risky and I cannot afford a bad year.

My main 5 mu is wheat-maize double cropping. That is our foundation. I plant winter wheat around October 10th. I buy the improved seed from the supply shop in town — about 15 jin per mu, costs me roughly 30 yuan per mu. Before planting I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu as a base, and then at green-up in March I topdress with about half a bag of urea. I use roughly 16 jin of nitrogen per mu in total. The extension agent once told me I could use less, but two years ago I cut back on one field and the wheat turned yellow. I would rather spend a little more than risk losing yield. I irrigate three times: once before winter to help it settle, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. Pumping electricity costs about 30 to 40 yuan each time for the whole field. My husband and I handle all the wheat work ourselves. We do not hire labor for it.

The summer maize goes in right after wheat harvest, around June 15th. The window is very tight — sometimes only three or four days. I hire the custom planter from our village because we cannot plant 5 mu fast enough by hand with just family labor. That costs about 80 yuan for the job. The hybrid maize seed is expensive, about 40 yuan per mu, but everyone knows you cannot save seed from hybrid corn — it does not grow right the second year. I put down fertilizer with the planter, one application of about 14 jin of nitrogen per mu. Last year the rains were okay so I only irrigated once, at flowering. If it is dry like three years ago, I will pump a second time. I spray herbicide once and insecticide if I see armyworm.

I have 2 mu of cotton. I plant it in late April. Cotton is our cash crop but it is picky — you have to watch for bollworm. I spray five times: herbicide once at the start, then insecticide four times through the summer. I put fertilizer down twice, once before planting and again when it flowers. I irrigate twice, at budding and at flowering. Picking is the hardest part. My daughter-in-law and I do most of it by hand, but when the bolls all open together in September we hire women from the next village for a few days. They charge 80 yuan per day but we have no choice — if you leave cotton in the field too long the quality drops.

My 1 mu of watermelon is on the sandy corner plot near the well. The soil there drains fast. My brother-in-law suggested watermelon years ago and it brings good money in July and August when we sell by the roadside. I buy seedlings now — it costs about 85 yuan per mu but it is easier than raising my own. I put a lot of chicken manure on that plot in spring, then some compound fertilizer when the vines start running. Watermelon likes potassium, so I make sure to give it enough. I irrigate four times because the sand dries out fast. The family manages all the watermelon work — planting, pruning, pollinating, and harvesting. I do not hire anyone for it.

All together I will spend about 3,200 yuan on seeds, fertilizer, pesticides, irrigation electricity, and hired labor this year. That is most of what my son sends home. If fertilizer prices go up, I will probably cut back on the cotton first. The wheat and maize I cannot reduce — we need that grain.
